note: A second round-1 review ran concurrently with the one recorded in pr18-r1.json, because two pr-loop orchestrators were driving PR #18 at the same time. Most of its findings duplicate pr18-r1.json. Only the additive ones are kept here so nothing is lost. The full 8-finding second pass is preserved in git at commit 6310e2c.

routing_conflict.resolution: defer to the more conservative routing — repair

additive_findings.claim: In light mode, hovering an item row drops title and badge text to 4.33:1 — below AA, and a regression from 4.77:1 in the palette this diff replaced.
additive_findings.acceptance: --dim on --muted and on the aria-current amber wash is >= 4.5:1 in both schemes.
additive_findings.relation: pr18-r1 R11 covers dark-mode hover VISIBILITY (1.09:1 change); this is the light-mode AA FAILURE, a different defect on the same selector.

additive_findings.claim: Beyond the two categories pr18-r1 R1 names, three further text/ground pairs fail the published minima, one of them only because of an opacity the measurement excluded.
additive_findings.evidence: `.s-unsupported,.s-failed` dark = 4.99:1; `.b.st-missing` on --panel dark = 5.13:1; `#banner .src{opacity:.85}` = 3.92:1 dark on the failed banner and 3.69:1 light on the success banner.
additive_findings.acceptance: Any check backing the contrast claim composites opacity and color-mix grounds, not just flat token pairs.
additive_findings.relation: extends pr18-r1 R1 with three concrete pairs and the opacity blind spot.

additive_findings.claim: While a fetch is in flight all three Extract buttons are disabled and their labels drop to 2.20:1 light / 3.20:1 dark.
additive_findings.evidence: index.html `button:disabled{opacity:.5}` composited over --bg; busy(true) disables every button for the fetch duration.
additive_findings.acceptance: Disabled buttons keep a legible label, or the busy state is acknowledged as intentionally illegible.
additive_findings.relation: not present in pr18-r1. WCAG 1.4.3 exempts disabled controls, so legibility not conformance.
